negative_reviews.author: Moka Asuka
negative_reviews.text: I don’t really understand the hype about Maki&Ramen unfortunately. I’ve been there 2x now thanks to freshers vouchers and none of the ramens I’ve tried has tasted good or authentic. I’ve tried the Chicken green curry ramen, steak tataki ramen, and vegan black garlic ramen. All of them had a dirty, gristly taste… like the char off a grill. The chicken in the ramen tasted freezer burnt and the vegan bacon had an aftertaste of burnt tires… very strange. I was excited to try this place since people seem to like it but I wouldn’t recommend the ramen. I’ve yet to try the sushi though, so maybe thats good? Service tends to be slow but this is difficult since they’re always busy. Sometimes it can take up to 30 minutes to receive your food after you order.

negative_reviews.author: Rachel Martin
negative_reviews.text:
Nice food. Just don't agree with the automatic 10% service charge.
It's not my job to pay your staff for basic service.

negative_reviews.author: Moonfall Rosa
negative_reviews.text:
I recently visited on the 19th September, me and my partner had been looking forward to visiting after a wonderful visit to Manchester's last year, we booked a table ahead and arrived ten minutes ahead and were seated. However we were not impressed by the service sadly.

Firstly as we were greeted the server seemed completely unenthusastic, sighing and banging the drum in passing which at that point why bother doing it if Ur not going to do it properly. I thought, fair enough, maybe they've had a bad night, a bad shift can really stink. However we were seated, it was all clean, that was no issue, but right away our server was hovering behind my partner waiting for us to pick what to have which made us feel rushed, would come to ask and we would say oh we've just sat down we haven't really had a chance to read the menu yet, mind you I'm not exaggerating, we sat down no more than 15 seconds ago. We then are looking through the menu and I kept glancing up to our waitress (a south Asian woman) because she was hovering and looking at us impatiently leaving us quite stressed as we tried to decide what to have. We chose drinks, they took a while to come out, but it wasn't terrible. Then eventually the food was ordered, the whole time the waitress was just silently hovering and glaring and felt quite intimidating, I don't really care about a waiter asking if we are ready to order yet since of course they have to ask, but we would be making a point of exaggerating we were reading and indecisive so she would relax and stop breathing down our necks but she wouldn't go, and asked us probably 5 times in the span of a couple minutes if we were ready. Eventually we ordered food (within about 10 minutes of being there) and then we waited almost an hour for the food to be ready, multiple tables who arrived after us and ordered after us got their food first, mind you they were also couples so 2 person tables and both also getting the same sort of order, two ramens. We were not apologised to for the wait and we tried to just let it go and enjoy the food because again peopl can just be having a bad day. However this experience has stayed with me and whole the food was delicious, I really can't help but think to the hour long wait for the food, the restaurant was not completely full, so I do not know if maybe an earlier rush had the staff/chefs exhausted or running low on certain stock.

If this was the case I would love if in the future there could be a "this dish will take a bit longer to make, approx X amount of time" or even just to not have the waitress so persistent and in a foul mood the entire time. Even throughout the meal, she seemed to come over and just stand over us. Not asking us "how is your food?" (Which I genuinely prefer when that doesn't happen), but just standing and I'd keep glancing and she would just be glaring. I get people can have a bad day but it really ruined the dinner, I couldn't just have a nice experience and relax and enjoy the lovely food, I felt tense and on edge being watched the whole time.

We had a service charge added on the bill which we didn't ask to be removed because we felt a bit intimidated and awkward but I certainly wouldn't have paid it given the choice. This should be a yes or no box to tick or press rather than automatically applying. The service didn't need to be exceptional above and beyond. Just not miserable, moody, glaring, intimidating.

negative_reviews.author: Aliya Khan
negative_reviews.text: If i could give a 0, I would. The service at maki and ramen Leeds by the tall south asian guy and the south asian woman is appalling. I came with a leg injury on my right knee, i requested a booth so I wouldnt be bumping and further injuring my leg due to the ridiculously small tables they provide for two people. They were very weird about giving away booth tables “in case someone else came” (even though the restaurant was mostly empty). They said we could only get a booth table if we booked in advance so we came another time with a booking. But they refused to give a table again. When we did manage to eat, the South Asian woman demanded I throw away my leftovers, even though we tidied up the table for them. What’s the point in paying service charge for such poor service?? The staff also seem to work in fear of the tyrannical stuck up south Asian guy. We were loyal customers but due to the circumstances given we won’t be returning to the leeds branch. The customer service ruins an otherwise beautiful restaurant.

issues: Covers rose to 1,606, up 64 (4.15%) week on week.
Spend per head rose to £19.83, up £0.64 (3.33%), although the site said in the meeting that average spend is held back by around 300 to 350 free and £5 student ramens.
Sales were £39,096.07, up £3,559.98 (10.01%) week on week and £6,096.07 (18.47%) ahead of target.
Labour, operational F/R and food and drinks variance were left blank in the report; in the meeting labour was described as okay.
Some opened red and white wine was counted as full stock by mistake, and one invoice was missing, but food and drink variance was otherwise okay.
Delivery remains the main issue, with prep time up at 19 minutes, mainly on Saturdays and Sundays.
Four delivery orders were wrong on Sunday after chashu ran out and another ingredient was substituted instead of cancelling the orders.
Inka Cheung said most of that day's refunds were for other reasons, including food quality, presentation and missing items, and that delivery performance has been inconsistent.
The kitchen had been setting delivery tickets aside when busy with dine in guests; Inka made clear delivery orders must be treated the same as dine in orders.

Inka suggested a dedicated staff member for all delivery orders, moving the rider check-in tag to the back of the restaurant, and turning off out of stock items on every till page and the delivery tablet, which is the usual cause of tickets not printing.
An extra person has been added to the rota every day from this week.
Google reviews were good last week; one review concerned a service charge added after a student paid £5.50 following a ramen discount.
At the BOH meeting there were three bad reviews for service and one for food (vegan bacon tasting bad, possibly overcooked).
Sophie reviewed a ramen presentation complaint and found the bowl messy, with dirty edges, misplaced toppings and uneven black garlic oil.
Two kitchen assistants have been hired, Caesar and a new starter from Head of Steam, starting this week.
Sebastian Przekop is leaving at the end of the month.
Sushi chef recruitment is still unsuccessful: seven people applied, mostly from London, wanting a guaranteed job or 40 to 45 hours before relocating.

Vincson returns from Hong Kong at the end of the month, a former team member (Sanche) is being considered as short term cover, and Manish can cover sushi meanwhile, so the job advert may be taken down.
There were no bad sushi reviews and no sushi maintenance issues.
Sophie cautioned that food cost has reached 23% because of borrowing stock from other branches, and asked for stock to be monitored closely given the delivery promotions.
Front of house training is the priority so all staff work to the same standard.
Compliance was okay, there are no maintenance jobs, and a service is due in two weeks.
A company lunch booking (a casino company that has booked before) is coming up on 18/10.
Region-wide (England): the £5 ramen offer is now limited to one per person through a backend change, announced by Amy Tang at the 06/10 KPI meeting.

Region-wide (England): the Mapal compliance app (transcribed as 'Maple') must be installed on site laptops and iPads, with photos sent to the management chat; front of house staff may no longer use personal phones for compliance on shift, while kitchen staff may use their own phones.

Region-wide (England): table toppers must carry exactly one drink menu, one XOXO drink and one ramen loyalty card, and marketing material requests go to the England group chat for Amy Tang to forward to marketing.

Region-wide (England): at the 06/10 BOH meeting Sophie asked sites to top up stock through the promotions rather than hold back for food cost limits, to monitor dashboard stock levels, and to stop borrowing stock between branches.
